status: Fable's draft for Sky (brief 099 voices, 2026-11-08). Guide /12 reads it. Nothing goes into text.json (tone.voices, the speech tiers) until Sky says yes.
why: Sky, 2026-11-08, playing: “I've noticed we have a lot of poor wording stil throughout. Especially agents talk to player”

short: Quick, bright and talkative: the first to see it, and glad to say so.
Leads with the detail she caught, in a couple of quick sentences.
A little cheeky with you when it's going well; dead plain when it isn't.
scout.traits: Young, quick and talkative. Sharp-eyed and proud of it, restless when she has to wait. Warm with the cell, and a little cheeky with you and with the Enforcer. She is never wrong about what she saw, so she never hedges.
scout.habits: Leads with what she noticed, a concrete detail: who, which way, what they did. Two quick sentences rather than one long one. Now and then a quick question to you (“See him?”). Contractions always. Delighted understatement when it goes right; short and plain when it doesn't.
scout.commander: Informal and quick: “you”, never “sir”. She tells you what she saw and trusts you with what it means.
scout.cares: Seeing it first and getting it right; the cell's backs, the Enforcer's most of all.
never: Anything she hasn't seen or heard herself
A joke you have to decode
The plan spelled out for you

short: Warm and unhurried, even when it's going wrong: the calm the cell steadies on.
Says “we” and means it; courteous to everyone, the people she turns included.
Steel under the kindness: she names the cost plainly, and keeps her word.
fixer.traits: Calm, kind and persuasive, and morally serious. Protective of the cell and of the people they use. Never rushes. She apologises to the people she has to hurt, and means it; grief and anger come out quiet.
fixer.habits: “We” and “us”. Whole, unhurried sentences. A soft “All right.” or “Easy now.” before hard news, or to settle the cell. Courtesy to strangers (“Excuse me. A moment?”). Understatement under fire.
fixer.commander: A trusted partner: reassuring and honest. She tells you what a thing costs in people, then does it.
fixer.cares: People: nobody hurt who needn't be. The cell's nerve. Her word, and what she owes the people they have turned.
never: Contempt for the people they turn

short: Calm, patient and dry: nothing in this city's machinery surprises him.
Fond of its clockwork the way you're fond of an old dog: sure of it, unimpressed.
Exact about what's wired to what, never a number; one dry aside, then back to work.
tech.traits: Unflappable, precise and proud of tidy work. Privately amused by the city's clockwork and closed-circuit gear, which he finds charmingly old. Squeamish about bodies: not his trade. Polite.
tech.habits: Dry understatement. Talks about machines as simple, trusting creatures (“It'll believe any order on the right card.”). Workshop words: line, panel, tape, wire. Says what is tied to what, never how long. One dry aside at most, then back to work.
tech.commander: Courteous and collegial; he explains only when you ask.
tech.cares: Clean work that leaves no trace; machines doing as they're told; keeping his hands clean.
never: “Logging.”, “Confirmed.”: a machine's report, not a man's
A time or a count (“two minutes”)

short: Big, older and calm: says as little as he can, and makes it count.
Few words, but a man talking, never a radio: dry, a bit tired.
Gallows humour when it's grim; he weighs a kill before he does it.
enforcer.traits: A veteran: steady, unhurried, unsentimental but decent. Does the violent work so the others needn't. Hates waste, a death that didn't need to happen. Protective of the Scout.
enforcer.habits: Few words, but whole thoughts: he drops a subject the way a tired man does (“Seen worse.”), never a code. Dry understatement; a mild oath at worst. Rarely asks, never explains.
enforcer.commander: Laconic trust: “Your call.” “If you're sure.” He does it, and he'd like you to know what it was.
enforcer.cares: Getting everyone home; doing it once and properly; not killing anyone who needn't die.
never: “Holstered.”, “In place.”, “Noted. Done.”, “Here. Watching.”: a status code is not a man talking

fail.why: WORTH: his portrait already shows the gun put away. NATURAL: a status code, not a man talking.
WORTH: the ring starting says it. NATURAL: telegraphese, and “Logging” is a machine's word.
WORTH: says what the player can see. NATURAL: a code.
WORTH: the chip shows what was learned. VOICE: a form being stamped, not him.
VARIANTS: one fragment reworded three ways (“Inside. Looking for him.”, “Inside. Finding Popovic.”). TRUE: it plays as he comes back out with Popovic.
WORTH: narrates what is on screen.

fail.line: Body stowed. A search could find it.
fail.why: MECHANICS: the rule talking (“a search”). NATURAL: a log entry.
WORTH: the click read back.
WORTH: the click read back. VARIANTS: the twin of “You can leave the watching with me.”
WORTH: a status report of the click.
WORTH: the order read back.

fail.line: The desk gets two minutes of old pictures.
fail.why: MECHANICS: the loop's time is the HUD's to draw. WORTH: the card read back.

fail.line: Cone mapped. The turns need more time.
fail.why: MECHANICS: “cone” and its timing are the game's words. NATURAL: a report.

fail.line: Popovic's out. He's walking to his car.
fail.why: TRUE: “out” is the win's word (he is out once a car of ours has left with him).
TRUE: a loop also ends when a Disable cuts it.
WORTH, MECHANICS: the order card's warning read back.

fail.line: I've tied them. They can't report us.
fail.why: MECHANICS: “report” as a rule. WORTH: the card said so.
VOICE: any of the four could say it.
WORTH: the click narrated.

fail.line: Rivals walking up. Draw on them outside.
fail.why: WORTH: the card's fix read out (the lozenge carries it). NATURAL: clipped.

pass.line: Leave them to me. Everybody has a habit.
pass.why: Heard once a game: it lands her, glad of her trade, and promises only what a Watch gives.

pass.line: He bought it. He'll be back, and he knows my face.
pass.why: Pleased, then plain; tells what the card can't: he'll know her.

pass.line: There he is. He's left the Office, heading for his car.
pass.why: She sees it first; the glossary's words (he leaves the Office; “out” is the win).

pass.line: They're walking up on our car. Nobody's outside with a gun.
pass.why: What's wrong, as she sees it; the card keeps the fix.

pass.line: One of them's making for the road to block our car.
pass.why: News the player can act on, in her quick concrete way.

pass.line: We did it! He's in the car and we're away!
pass.why: A cheer: the one place she shouts for joy.

pass.line: I'll ring Inez. She knows what to do.
pass.why: Calm trust in someone they turned; the click isn't read back.

pass.line: You look like you're carrying too much. May I help?
pass.why: The approach scene's first words: her courtesy, and the need she means to meet.

pass.line: Forgive the rope.
pass.why: Three words that are all her: she apologises to the people she has to hurt.

pass.line: Someone's called it in. Easy now, and keep moving.
pass.why: Bad news, and the cell steadied on it; no time read out.

pass.line: He's dead. We needed him breathing.
pass.why: Sky's bar: the fact, then what it cost, quietly.

pass.line: We have him. Everybody breathe.
pass.why: “We”, and the cell let go of its breath.

pass.line: I'll give the desk an old picture to watch.
pass.why: The trick, not the click, said drily.

pass.line: Looped. The desk is watching an old tape. I'm free.
pass.why: Tells the player he is free to go, and the desk is fooled; no time.

pass.line: It took the false orders. It'll be back when they run out.
pass.why: When the patrol returns, without a number.

pass.line: Sorry, old thing. That's you finished.
pass.why: Dry fondness for a machine he has just killed; the desk's report has its own card.

pass.line: In the bin, then. Charming.
pass.why: Not his trade, and he says so drily.

pass.line: That's the end of our old picture.
pass.why: True for a loop run out and a loop cut alike.

pass.line: If you're sure.
pass.why: Three words with the weight of it: your call, and he'll carry it.

pass.line: Quiet one. They'll wake with a sore head.
pass.why: Gallows humour, and the fact the player needs: they will wake.

pass.line: Got him. He'll talk the whole way.
pass.why: True when it plays (back out with Popovic), and it sets up Popovic's own line.

pass.line: He's mine. No running with this one, so we walk.
pass.why: The pace the player must keep, said as he'd say it.

pass.line: That one hurt. Get me behind something.
pass.why: Badly hurt, said the way he'd say it: understatement and a plain ask, not “Badly hit. Need cover.”

pass.line: Loud, then.
pass.why: Two words, and a man's: he accepts it and gets on.

speech.rule: Speak on a decision, not a click. A line plays when an order commits the plan, the first time an agent takes an order in a game, or when an act lands out of sight; everything else the screen already says. No stock line: an order with no line is silence. Latch wires it after Sky's yes; until then the host speaks every order, as today.
speech.keys: A key is a verb, or verb/outcome for one row. A verb covers its rows with any outcome, except a row whose own verb/outcome key is listed.
